```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(stringr)
library(tibble)
library(psych)
library(ggplot2)
library(writexl)
library(forcats)
library(cluster)
library(factoextra)
library(NbClust)
library(mclust)
library(scales)

# Additional packages needed for the segment-quality assessment, the
# customer-to-segment assignment rules and the recommendation write-up
# added below (Sections 12-16).
new_needed <- c("fpc", "rpart", "rpart.plot", "knitr")
missing_needed <- new_needed[!new_needed %in% installed.packages()[, "Package"]]
if (length(missing_needed) > 0) install.packages(missing_needed, dependencies = TRUE)
library(fpc)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(knitr)

# NbClust/psych/mclust/fpc/rpart etc. each pull in dependencies (e.g. MASS)
# that define their OWN versions of common dplyr verb names, and those get
# attached to the search path AFTER dplyr's -- so a bare call later in the
# script can silently resolve to the wrong function instead of dplyr's. This
# is exactly what produced two different "unimplemented type 'list' in
# order()" crashes when this script was first built (once via a masked
# select()/filter(), once via a masked count()) -- the error looks like a
# data bug but is actually a name collision. Rather than fix verbs one at a
# time as each new one surfaces, force EVERY commonly-clobbered dplyr verb to
# resolve to dplyr's version, in the global environment, once, here -- after
# all libraries (including the ones added just above) have loaded.
dplyr_verbs <- c("select", "filter", "mutate", "arrange", "summarise",
                  "summarize", "group_by", "count", "distinct", "slice",
                  "rename", "bind_rows", "pull", "left_join", "inner_join",
                  "full_join", "anti_join", "semi_join")
for (v in dplyr_verbs) assign(v, get(v, envir = asNamespace("dplyr")))
rm(v, dplyr_verbs)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. CONFIGURATION
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- EDIT THIS PATH if the Reduction Stage output folder changes ---------
reduction_rds_path <- "workstream2d_outputs_hierarchical/hierarchical_reduction_objects.rds"
output_dir         <- "workstream2d_clustering_outputs_hierarchical"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(1526)

# THIS VARIANT (02d) has no FA-vs-PCA choice to make: 02d_Reduction_Stage_
# Hierarchical.Rmd produces exactly one combined score set (5 reliable FA
# factors from the 45-item WS1 pool + F1's + F3's + ProviderPerception's own
# within-block factors -- full 80-item coverage), not parallel FA/PCA
# alternatives. SCORE_SET is kept only so the downstream
# guards written for 02/02c (`identical(SCORE_SET, "fa")`, used to decide
# whether the hard-coded FACTOR_THEMES/persona labels or the raw-variable
# "Segment Defining Variables" mapping are safe to compute) continue to
# resolve to FALSE here via R's `&&` short-circuit evaluation, rather than
# silently reusing loadings/labels that don't apply to this hybrid score
# set. Do not set this to "fa" or "pca" in this script.
SCORE_SET <- "hierarchical"

HIER_METHOD    <- "ward.D2"   # Ward's minimum-variance criterion (Ward, 1963)
NBCLUST_MIN_K  <- 2
NBCLUST_MAX_K  <- 8           # range for Ward's NbClust battery + K-means elbow/silhouette plots
ENTROPY_MIN    <- 0.80        # classification-clarity threshold (Souza et al., 2019)
KMO_MIN        <- 0.60        # Kaiser (1974) floor -- same constant/citation as
                               # 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd's KMO_MIN; redefined
                               # here (added 2026-08-10) rather than imported, since this
                               # script only reads reduction_obj's SAVED combined_kmo value,
                               # not the Reduction script's own environment/constants -- used
                               # in Section 15 to interpret that saved KMO against the same
                               # floor it was checked against upstream.

# FIXED (2026-08-02, after first real knit-through): the GMM/LPA exploratory
# BIC search (Section 6) originally reused NBCLUST_MAX_K (8) as its own
# ceiling. On the first run, BIC was STILL FALLING at k=8 (14162 -> 14144 ->
# 14085 from k=6 to k=8) -- i.e. the search was cut off before finding
# where BIC actually bottoms out, so "k=8 selected" in that run was really
# "k=8 was the edge of the search window", not a genuine BIC minimum.
# Decoupled into its own, wider ceiling so the unconstrained GMM diagnostic
# gets a fair chance to find its true BIC minimum, without slowing down
# NbClust's 26-index battery (which does not need as wide a range and is
# already reasonably expensive at NBCLUST_MAX_K = 8).
GMM_MIN_K <- NBCLUST_MIN_K
GMM_MAX_K <- 15

SHORTLIST_K             <- 4:6
MIN_VIABLE_SEGMENT_PCT  <- 5    # segments below this share of respondents are
                                  # treated as too small to action commercially
DEFINING_NEED_Z         <- 0.30 # |standardised centroid| above which a need
                                  # factor is "defining" for a segment -- used
                                  # identically for all three methods now that
                                  # all three operate on the same continuous
                                  # factor-score representation
STABILITY_B_DIST        <- 50   # bootstrap reps, Ward's/K-means (fpc::clusterboot)
STABILITY_B_GMM         <- 30   # bootstrap reps, GMM/LPA (heavier per-rep cost --
                                  # increase for the final dissertation run if
                                  # runtime allows)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD REDUCTION-STAGE OBJECTS (combined hierarchical scores + firmographics)
#    THIS VARIANT (02d) consumes 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd's output
#    -- a two-stage design, not a flat pooled reduction: Stage 1 reuses
#    02c's 5 reliable FA factors from the 45-item WS1 pool (KMO=0.973)
#    unchanged, and separately runs its own within-block EFA for F1, F3, and
#    ProviderPerception (C5c_2r6 + F10r2/r3/r7/r15 -- the 5 items that were
#    previously excluded from every reduction in this pipeline family; F1/F3
#    are the two blocks that made the original 80-item pool's KMO collapse
#    to 0.153). Stage 2 combines all of those block-level factor scores into
#    one respondent-level continuous dataset -- so, unlike 02/02c, EVERY one
#    of the 80 raw items is now genuinely represented somewhere in this
#    clustering input (not merely 75, as in the prior version of this
#    script), never pooled into one single flat correlation matrix. See that script's
#    header and WS1_50Item_Needs_Register.xlsx for the full reasoning. It
#    exists alongside (not instead of) 02_Clustering.Rmd/02c_Clustering_
#    WS1Needs.Rmd so all three item-pool/design choices can be compared. This
#    script otherwise reuses the same method battery (Ward's/K-means/GMM-LPA
#    + composite quality scoring) unchanged, so the comparison isolates the
#    effect of the reduction design, not the clustering methodology. It does
#    not re-import/re-recode the raw survey file or re-run any EFA itself: it
#    consumes the Reduction Stage's saved respondent-level scores, respondent
#    identifier and firmographic extract directly.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(
  "Reduction Stage output not found -- knit 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd first" =
    file.exists(reduction_rds_path)
)
reduction_obj <- readRDS(reduction_rds_path)
stopifnot(
  "hierarchical_reduction_objects.rds is missing expected components -- re-knit 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd with the current version of that script" =
    all(c("combined_scores", "score_cols", "uuid", "firmographics") %in% names(reduction_obj))
)
# "score_item_map"/"score_reliability" are required as of the robustness-
# improvement pass (2026-08-05): they drive the real Segment Defining
# Variables mapping (Section 13c) and the ablation/sensitivity check
# (Section 13d) below. Both need a fresh knit of the current Reduction
# Stage script -- checked separately from the stopifnot above so the error
# message points the analyst at exactly what to re-knit.
stopifnot(
  "hierarchical_reduction_objects.rds predates the robustness-improvement pass -- re-knit the current 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd to generate score_item_map/score_reliability before knitting this script" =
    all(c("score_item_map", "score_reliability") %in% names(reduction_obj))
)
# This variant has no per-raw-variable FA loadings matrix spanning the whole
# combined score set (Stage 1 ran FOUR separate EFAs -- the 45-item pool's,
# F1's, F3's, and ProviderPerception's -- each with its own loadings matrix
# over a different item set, not one unified matrix). Rather than reconcile
# four loadings tables into one "Segment Defining Variables" mapping (a real
# but separate piece of work), that section is left to degrade gracefully
# via the SCORE_SET guard below, exactly as the existing 02c code already
# does when its own validity checks fail -- no behaviour needed here beyond
# not claiming "fa"/"pca" as SCORE_SET (see Section 0).
has_item_labels <- FALSE
# IMPORTANT: this must check for the exact name "factor_reliability", not
# "f1_reliability"/"f3_reliability"/"pp_reliability" -- Section 13b's lookup
# code below reads `reduction_obj$factor_reliability` literally (inherited
# unchanged from 02c), and that single unified component does not exist in
# this RDS (Stage 1 produced three SEPARATE reliability tables instead, one
# per block). Since "factor_reliability" is genuinely absent, this correctly
# evaluates FALSE, which routes Section 13b to its existing NA-fallback
# branch instead of crashing on `reduction_obj$factor_reliability$factor`
# (NULL) being matched against a non-empty `num_cols`. The three real
# reliability tables are still printed here for the console/report, just not
# wired into that lookup.
has_factor_reliability <- "factor_reliability" %in% names(reduction_obj)
cat("F1 block factor reliability:\n"); print(reduction_obj$f1_reliability)
cat("F3 block factor reliability:\n"); print(reduction_obj$f3_reliability)
cat("ProviderPerception block factor reliability:\n"); print(reduction_obj$pp_reliability)

cat("Loaded reduction-stage objects:", nrow(reduction_obj$combined_scores), "respondents,",
    length(reduction_obj$score_cols), "combined block-level scores:",
    paste(reduction_obj$score_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Stage 2 (combined-score) suitability, from the Reduction Stage: KMO =",
    round(reduction_obj$combined_kmo, 3), "\n")

firmo <- reduction_obj$firmographics %>%
  mutate(S2 = as.numeric(S2), S3 = as.numeric(S3))
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. BUILD THE CLUSTERING INPUT MATRIX
#    Column names are kept exactly as the Reduction Stage produced them
#    (NeedFA1-5, F1_FactorN, F3_FactorN) rather than renamed to a generic
#    FA1..FAk sequence -- there is no single unified factor solution here to
#    number that way, and the descriptive names make every downstream table
#    (segment profiles, defining-variable lists) self-explanatory without
#    needing a separate lookup.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
continuous_input <- reduction_obj$combined_scores
num_cols <- reduction_obj$score_cols

n_missing <- sum(is.na(continuous_input[num_cols]))
cat("Clustering input: ", nrow(continuous_input), "respondents x", length(num_cols),
    "combined hierarchical scores (", n_missing, "missing cells)\n")
stopifnot(
  "Clustering input has unexpected missing cells -- the Reduction Stage's combine step should leave 0 missing here" =
    n_missing == 0
)

continuous_scaled <- scale(as.matrix(continuous_input[, num_cols]))
rownames(continuous_scaled) <- continuous_input$uuid

# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): no multivariate outlier screening was
# previously run before Euclidean-distance clustering (Ward's linkage in
# particular is sensitive to outliers). This is not a scan-and-remove step --
# no respondents are dropped -- just an explicit, auditable check so an
# unusually influential respondent (e.g. one riding a poorly-conditioned
# block's noisy factor score -- see the F3 condition-number warning in the
# Reduction Stage) is visible before it can silently shape cluster boundaries.
outlier_flags <- rowSums(abs(continuous_scaled) > 3) > 0
n_outliers <- sum(outlier_flags)
cat("Respondents with |z|>3 on at least one clustering-input factor score:",
    n_outliers, "of", nrow(continuous_scaled),
    paste0("(", round(100 * n_outliers / nrow(continuous_scaled), 1), "%)"), "\n")
if (n_outliers > 0) {
  cat("These respondents are NOT removed (Ward's/K-means/GMM below all still run on the full",
      "sample) -- flagged so their influence on segment boundaries can be checked if a",
      "solution looks driven by a small number of extreme cases.\n")
}
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. DESCRIPTIVE CHECK OF THE CLUSTERING INPUTS
#    ("Analyse survey responses" -- WBS Workstream 2 brief). Run before any
#    clustering so scale, spread and redundancy issues are caught before
#    they distort a distance-based solution. Redundancy is expected to be
#    lower here than with raw-item inputs, since these are already reduced,
#    largely orthogonal-by-construction factor scores (oblimin for the 5
#    need factors, varimax within the F1 and F3 blocks) rather than raw
#    items -- but cross-stage correlation (e.g. a need factor correlating
#    with an F1/F3 block factor) is checked, not assumed, since Stage 1's
#    three EFAs were run completely independently of one another.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
describe_needs <- psych::describe(continuous_input[, num_cols]) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("need_variable") %>%
  select(need_variable, n, mean, sd, min, max, skew, kurtosis)
cat("Descriptive statistics for the", length(num_cols), "clustering-input factor scores:\n")
print(describe_needs)

needs_cor <- cor(continuous_scaled, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
high_cor_pairs <- which(abs(needs_cor) > 0.8 & upper.tri(needs_cor), arr.ind = TRUE)
if (nrow(high_cor_pairs) > 0) {
  cat("\nWARNING: the following factor-score pairs correlate above |0.8| -- ",
      "consider whether the oblique rotation is leaving near-duplicate factors:\n")
  print(data.frame(var1 = rownames(needs_cor)[high_cor_pairs[, 1]],
                    var2 = colnames(needs_cor)[high_cor_pairs[, 2]],
                    r = round(needs_cor[high_cor_pairs], 2)))
} else {
  cat("\nNo factor-score pairs correlate above |0.8| -- no evidence of redundant ",
      "clustering inputs distorting the distance metric.\n")
}

## FIGURE: correlation heatmap of every clustering-input factor score.
if (requireNamespace("corrplot", quietly = TRUE)) {
  corrplot::corrplot(needs_cor, method = "color", type = "upper", tl.cex = 0.8,
                      tl.col = "black", order = "hclust",
                      title = "Clustering-Input Factor-Score Correlation Matrix", mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
} else {
  heatmap(needs_cor, symm = TRUE, main = "Clustering-Input Factor-Score Correlation Matrix")
}
dev.copy(png, file.path(output_dir, "needs_correlation_heatmap.png"), width = 900, height = 800)
invisible(dev.off())

write.csv(describe_needs, file.path(output_dir, "Needs_Descriptive_Statistics.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

TABLE: descriptive statistics for every clustering-input factor score.

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
print(knitr::kable(describe_needs, digits = 2,
                    caption = "Descriptive statistics: clustering-input factor scores"))
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. WARD'S HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING -- EXPLORATORY / UNCONSTRAINED PASS
#    (STAGE 1 -- fixes k and starting centroids for the confirmatory
#    K-means run in Section 5). This pass lets NbClust pick whatever k the
#    internal validity indices favour with no constraint; Section 11 below
#    separately generates a 4-6 segment shortlist regardless of what k this
#    unconstrained diagnostic settles on, per the WBS brief's requirement
#    for a commercially actionable 4-6 segment solution.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
dist_mat <- dist(continuous_scaled, method = "euclidean")
hc_ward  <- hclust(dist_mat, method = HIER_METHOD)

## FIGURE: full dendrogram (rendered inline, then saved to file).
plot(hc_ward, labels = FALSE, main = "Ward's Hierarchical Clustering (Euclidean distance)",
     xlab = "", sub = "")
dev.copy(png, file.path(output_dir, "dendrogram.png"), width = 1200, height = 700)
invisible(dev.off())

# NbClust majority-rule across its full battery of internal validity
# indices -- avoids anchoring the cluster-count decision on a single index.
set.seed(1526)
nb <- NbClust::NbClust(data = continuous_scaled, distance = "euclidean",
                        min.nc = NBCLUST_MIN_K, max.nc = NBCLUST_MAX_K,
                        method = HIER_METHOD, index = "all")

# GUARDRAIL (added 2026-08-03, after the raw-items robustness-check script
# turned up 3 impossible votes -- k=0 x2, k=1 x1 -- in an otherwise identical
# NbClust call on 80-dimensional data): a handful of NbClust's ~26 internal
# indices can return an out-of-range/placeholder code instead of a genuine
# k within [min.nc, max.nc], apparently under numerical strain from high
# dimensionality or edge-case index behaviour. `table(nb$Best.nc[1, ])` was
# tallying these alongside real votes with no filter -- harmless while the
# real majority is decisive, but a latent risk in a closer-margin run.
# Filter to the valid, configured k range before tallying, and flag (not
# silently drop) anything excluded so it stays auditable.
raw_best_nc <- nb$Best.nc[1, ]
invalid_votes <- raw_best_nc[!raw_best_nc %in% NBCLUST_MIN_K:NBCLUST_MAX_K]
if (length(invalid_votes) > 0) {
  cat("WARNING:", length(invalid_votes), "NbClust index(es) returned a k",
      "outside the configured [", NBCLUST_MIN_K, ",", NBCLUST_MAX_K,
      "] range -- excluded from the majority-vote tally:\n")
  # useNA = "ifany": table() drops NA by default, which would silently
  # under-report this breakdown relative to the length() count above
  # whenever an index fails to compute at all (returns NA) rather than an
  # out-of-range number -- exactly what happened in the raw-items script's
  # first post-fix run (6 invalid votes by length(), but only 3 accounted
  # for by table() before this change, because 3 were NA rather than 0/1).
  print(table(invalid_votes, useNA = "ifany"))
}
k_votes <- table(raw_best_nc[raw_best_nc %in% NBCLUST_MIN_K:NBCLUST_MAX_K])
cat("NbClust index votes by k (valid range only):\n"); print(k_votes)

# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): the guardrail above filters out-of-range
# votes but doesn't confirm nothing else went missing -- e.g. an index that
# errored internally and was silently excluded from nb$Best.nc altogether,
# rather than returning an explicit out-of-range/NA code. Reconcile the
# valid-vote count against the total number of indices NbClust attempted
# (ncol(nb$Best.nc)) so a silent additional loss is visible, not assumed away.
n_indices_total <- ncol(nb$Best.nc)
n_accounted <- sum(k_votes) + length(invalid_votes)
cat("NbClust index reconciliation:", n_accounted, "of", n_indices_total,
    "indices accounted for (valid votes + flagged invalid votes).\n")
if (n_accounted != n_indices_total) {
  cat("WARNING:", n_indices_total - n_accounted, "index(es) are unaccounted for -- neither a",
      "valid vote nor a flagged invalid vote. Some index likely failed silently; investigate",
      "nb$Best.nc directly before treating the majority-rule k as fully audited.\n")
}

k_hier <- as.integer(names(sort(k_votes, decreasing = TRUE))[1])
cat("\nSelected k (NbClust majority rule):", k_hier, "\n")

## FIGURE: NbClust's index votes, so the majority-rule pick is visually
## auditable rather than a single printed number.
barplot(k_votes, col = "steelblue4",
        main = "NbClust: number of indices favouring each k",
        xlab = "Number of clusters (k)", ylab = "Number of indices")
dev.copy(png, file.path(output_dir, "nbclust_votes.png"), width = 900, height = 600)
invisible(dev.off())

ward_clusters <- cutree(hc_ward, k = k_hier)
ward_centroids <- t(sapply(sort(unique(ward_clusters)), function(cl) {
  colMeans(continuous_scaled[ward_clusters == cl, , drop = FALSE])
}))

## FIGURE: dendrogram with the chosen k-cluster cut highlighted.
plot(hc_ward, labels = FALSE, main = paste0("Ward's Hierarchical Clustering -- k = ", k_hier, " cut"),
     xlab = "", sub = "")
rect.hclust(hc_ward, k = k_hier, border = "firebrick3")
dev.copy(png, file.path(output_dir, "dendrogram_cut.png"), width = 1200, height = 700)
invisible(dev.off())
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. K-MEANS (STAGE 2 -- confirmatory, seeded from Ward's centroids;
#    PLUS a random-start sensitivity check)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Confirmatory (two-stage) solution -- Muller & Hamm (2014) / Hair et al. (2010)
km_confirmatory <- kmeans(continuous_scaled, centers = ward_centroids, iter.max = 100)

# Sensitivity check: standard random-start K-means with the same k
set.seed(1526)
km_random <- kmeans(continuous_scaled, centers = k_hier, nstart = 25, iter.max = 100)

ari_confirm_vs_random <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_confirmatory$cluster, km_random$cluster)
cat("Adjusted Rand Index, confirmatory (Ward-seeded) vs random-start K-means:",
    round(ari_confirm_vs_random, 3),
    "\n(closer to 1 = the confirmatory solution is not an artefact of seeding)\n")

sil_km <- cluster::silhouette(km_confirmatory$cluster, dist_mat)
cat("Confirmatory K-means mean silhouette width:", round(mean(sil_km[, 3]), 3), "\n")

## FIGURE: within-cluster sum-of-squares elbow.
p_wss <- factoextra::fviz_nbclust(continuous_scaled, kmeans, method = "wss", k.max = NBCLUST_MAX_K)
print(p_wss)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "elbow_wss.png"), p_wss, width = 9, height = 6)

## FIGURE: average silhouette width by k.
p_sil <- factoextra::fviz_nbclust(continuous_scaled, kmeans, method = "silhouette", k.max = NBCLUST_MAX_K)
print(p_sil)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "elbow_silhouette.png"), p_sil, width = 9, height = 6)

## FIGURE: 2-D PCA projection of respondents, coloured by K-means
## (confirmatory) cluster.
pca_needs <- prcomp(continuous_scaled, scale. = FALSE)
pca_var_pct <- round(100 * summary(pca_needs)$importance[2, 1:2], 1)
pca_df <- tibble(
  PC1 = pca_needs$x[, 1], PC2 = pca_needs$x[, 2],
  cluster = as.factor(km_confirmatory$cluster)
)
p_pca_km <- ggplot2::ggplot(pca_df, ggplot2::aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = cluster)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "K-means (confirmatory) solution -- PCA projection of respondents",
                x = paste0("PC1 (", pca_var_pct[1], "% variance)"),
                y = paste0("PC2 (", pca_var_pct[2], "% variance)"),
                colour = "Cluster") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_pca_km)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "kmeans_pca_scatter.png"), p_pca_km, width = 8, height = 6)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. GAUSSIAN MIXTURE MODEL / LATENT PROFILE ANALYSIS
#    (continuous-data analogue of Latent Class Analysis)
#    poLCA-style LCA requires categorical manifest variables; this script's
#    clustering inputs are now continuous FA/PCA factor scores (Section 2),
#    so the probabilistic/model-based third method is Latent Profile
#    Analysis -- a finite Gaussian mixture model fit to continuous
#    indicators (Vermunt & Magidson, 2002; Oberski, 2016) -- implemented via
#    mclust::Mclust(), which additionally selects the best-fitting
#    covariance structure (spherical/diagonal/ellipsoidal, equal or varying
#    across classes) by BIC rather than assuming one shape. This mirrors the
#    earlier categorical-LCA step this script used before the client's pivot as
#    closely as the change in variable type allows: probabilistic class
#    membership, entropy-based classification clarity, and BIC-based class-
#    count selection are all retained.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
calc_entropy <- function(posterior) {
  p <- posterior
  p[p == 0] <- 1e-10   # avoid log(0)
  raw_entropy <- -sum(p * log(p))
  n <- nrow(posterior)
  k <- ncol(posterior)
  1 - raw_entropy / (n * log(k))
}

gmm_fit_table <- purrr::map_dfr(GMM_MIN_K:GMM_MAX_K, function(k) {
  fit <- tryCatch(mclust::Mclust(continuous_scaled, G = k), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(fit)) {
    return(tibble(nclass = k, N = NA_integer_, npar = NA_integer_, loglik = NA_real_,
                  BIC = NA_real_, AIC = NA_real_, entropy = NA_real_, model = NA_character_))
  }
  n_obs <- fit$n
  npar  <- fit$df
  ll    <- fit$loglik
  # mclust's own $bic component uses the OPPOSITE sign convention to poLCA's
  # (mclust: higher = better, = 2*loglik - npar*log(n)); recomputed here in
  # the conventional "lower = better" form used for AIC/BIC everywhere else
  # in this pipeline, to avoid a sign-convention mix-up when comparing.
  bic_std <- -2 * ll + npar * log(n_obs)
  aic_std <- -2 * ll + 2 * npar
  ent <- calc_entropy(fit$z)
  tibble(nclass = k, N = n_obs, npar = npar, loglik = ll,
         BIC = bic_std, AIC = aic_std, entropy = round(ent, 3), model = fit$modelName)
})
cat("GMM/LPA model comparison across class counts:\n")
print(gmm_fit_table)

## FIGURE: BIC by class count.
plot(gmm_fit_table$nclass, gmm_fit_table$BIC, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Number of classes", ylab = "BIC (lower = better fit)",
     main = "GMM/LPA class-count fit (BIC)")
dev.copy(png, file.path(output_dir, "gmm_fit.png"), width = 1000, height = 600)
invisible(dev.off())

# Selection rule: lowest BIC among class counts meeting the entropy >= 0.80
# classification-clarity threshold (Souza et al., 2019); fall back to the
# global BIC minimum if no class count clears that bar, flagging the
# fallback explicitly so it gets scrutinised rather than silently accepted.
eligible <- gmm_fit_table %>% filter(entropy >= ENTROPY_MIN, !is.na(BIC))
if (nrow(eligible) > 0) {
  k_gmm <- eligible$nclass[which.min(eligible$BIC)]
  cat("\nSelected GMM/LPA class count (min BIC subject to entropy >=", ENTROPY_MIN, "):", k_gmm, "\n")
} else {
  k_gmm <- gmm_fit_table$nclass[which.min(gmm_fit_table$BIC)]
  cat("\nWARNING: no class count reached entropy >=", ENTROPY_MIN,
      "-- falling back to global BIC minimum:", k_gmm,
      "-- inspect classification clarity before treating this as final.\n")
}

gmm_final <- mclust::Mclust(continuous_scaled, G = k_gmm)

## FIGURE: profile heatmap for the selected GMM/LPA model -- centroid (mean
## z-score per factor per class), the continuous-data equivalent of the
## item-response-probability heatmap this script used for LCA previously.
gmm_profile <- as.data.frame(t(gmm_final$parameters$mean)) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("class") %>%
  mutate(class = paste0("Class ", class))
gmm_profile_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(gmm_profile, cols = -class, names_to = "need", values_to = "z")
p_gmm_heat <- ggplot2::ggplot(gmm_profile_long, ggplot2::aes(x = need, y = class, fill = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue4", mid = "white", high = "firebrick3", midpoint = 0) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("GMM/LPA (", k_gmm, "-class) profile: mean factor score (z) by class"),
                x = "Need factor", y = "Class", fill = "z-score") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_gmm_heat)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "gmm_profile_heatmap.png"), p_gmm_heat, width = 8, height = 5)
```

assignments <- tibble(

  comparison = c("Ward's vs K-means (confirmatory)",
                  "Ward's vs GMM/LPA",
                  "K-means (confirmatory) vs GMM/LPA"),
  adjusted_rand_index = c(
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(assignments$ward_cluster, assignments$kmeans_cluster),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(assignments$ward_cluster, assignments$gmm_class),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(assignments$kmeans_cluster, assignments$gmm_class)
  )
)
cat("\nCross-method triangulation (Adjusted Rand Index, Hubert & Arabie, 1985):\n")
print(ari_table)

## FIGURE: cross-tabulation heatmaps between each pair of solutions.
plot_crosstab_heatmap <- function(data, col_a, col_b, label_a, label_b) {
  tab <- data %>% count(!!rlang::sym(col_a), !!rlang::sym(col_b), name = "n")
  names(tab)[1:2] <- c("a", "b")
  ggplot2::ggplot(tab, ggplot2::aes(x = as.factor(a), y = as.factor(b), fill = n)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile() +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = n), size = 3) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue4") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = paste(label_a, "vs", label_b), x = label_a, y = label_b, fill = "N") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
}
p_ct1 <- plot_crosstab_heatmap(assignments, "ward_cluster", "kmeans_cluster", "Ward's cluster", "K-means cluster")
p_ct2 <- plot_crosstab_heatmap(assignments, "ward_cluster", "gmm_class", "Ward's cluster", "GMM/LPA class")
p_ct3 <- plot_crosstab_heatmap(assignments, "kmeans_cluster", "gmm_class", "K-means cluster", "GMM/LPA class")
print(p_ct1); print(p_ct2); print(p_ct3)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "triangulation_ward_vs_kmeans.png"), p_ct1, width = 6, height = 5)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "triangulation_ward_vs_gmm.png"), p_ct2, width = 6, height = 5)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "triangulation_kmeans_vs_gmm.png"), p_ct3, width = 6, height = 5)

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. EXTERNAL VALIDATION AGAINST FIRMOGRAPHICS (NOT USED IN CLUSTERING)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
profiling <- assignments %>% left_join(firmo, by = "uuid")

validate_solution <- function(data, cluster_col, solution_label) {
  cl <- data[[cluster_col]]
  kw_s2 <- kruskal.test(data$S2 ~ as.factor(cl))
  kw_s3 <- kruskal.test(data$S3 ~ as.factor(cl))
  chi_s4 <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table(cl, data$S4)))
  chi_d3 <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(table(cl, data$D3)))
  tibble(
    solution = solution_label,
    test = c("Kruskal-Wallis: employees (S2)", "Kruskal-Wallis: sites (S3)",
             "Chi-square: sector (S4)", "Chi-square: turnover band (D3)"),
    statistic = c(kw_s2$statistic, kw_s3$statistic, chi_s4$statistic, chi_d3$statistic),
    p_value = c(kw_s2$p.value, kw_s3$p.value, chi_s4$p.value, chi_d3$p.value)
  )
}

firmo_validation <- bind_rows(
  validate_solution(profiling, "ward_cluster", "Ward's hierarchical"),
  validate_solution(profiling, "kmeans_cluster", "K-means (confirmatory)"),
  validate_solution(profiling, "gmm_class", "GMM/LPA")
)
cat("Firmographic external-validity tests (non-parametric; S2/S3 are ",
    "right-skewed counts, so Kruskal-Wallis is used in place of ANOVA):\n")
print(firmo_validation)
```
