The sections above (1-10) are exploratory: they let each method's own internal
validity indices pick whatever cluster/class count they favour with no
constraint, and triangulate/validate that unconstrained result. The sections
below implement the remaining WBS Workstream 2 activities that specifically
require a **commercially actionable, 4-6 segment** answer: segment quality
assessment (size, distinctiveness, stability, interpretability), shortlisting
and recommending a final 4-6 segment model, defining customer-to-segment
assignment rules, and a final rationale-and-limitations write-up.

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. SHORTLIST CANDIDATE SOLUTIONS AT k = 4, 5, 6
#     ("Identify clusters... using various clustering methodologies" +
#     "Define and recommend 4-6 needs-based customer segments shortlisted
#     from Workstream 1" -- WBS Workstream 2 brief). A candidate solution is
#     generated for EVERY method x k combination in the 4-6 range, so the
#     quality-assessment step below (Section 12) can compare all nine on a
#     like-for-like basis rather than assuming each method's unconstrained
#     optimum (Sections 4-6) is automatically the best 4-6-segment answer.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
generate_ward_kmeans <- function(k) {
  wc <- cutree(hc_ward, k = k)
  wcent <- t(sapply(sort(unique(wc)), function(cl) {
    colMeans(continuous_scaled[wc == cl, , drop = FALSE])
  }))
  km <- kmeans(continuous_scaled, centers = wcent, iter.max = 100)
  list(ward = wc, kmeans = km$cluster, kmeans_obj = km)
}
candidate_dist <- purrr::map(SHORTLIST_K, generate_ward_kmeans)
names(candidate_dist) <- paste0("k", SHORTLIST_K)

generate_gmm <- function(k) mclust::Mclust(continuous_scaled, G = k)
candidate_gmm <- purrr::map(SHORTLIST_K, generate_gmm)
names(candidate_gmm) <- paste0("k", SHORTLIST_K)

cat("Generated", length(SHORTLIST_K) * 3, "candidate solutions (",
    paste(SHORTLIST_K, collapse = ", "), "segments x Ward's/K-means/GMM-LPA)\n")
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. SEGMENT QUALITY ASSESSMENT -- SIZE, DISTINCTIVENESS, STABILITY,
#     INTERPRETABILITY ("Assess segment quality based on size,
#     distinctiveness, stability and interpretability" -- WBS Workstream 2
#     brief). Applied to all nine k=4-6 candidates from Section 11. Because
#     all three methods now share the same continuous factor-score
#     representation, distinctiveness (eta-squared) and interpretability
#     (defining-need count, DEFINING_NEED_Z) are computed IDENTICALLY for
#     all three -- unlike this script's earlier categorical-LCA version,
#     which had to combine LCA entropy and distance-based eta-squared on one
#     normalised scale as a documented limitation. Only the STABILITY
#     estimator still differs by method family: Jaccard co-membership
#     bootstrap for the two distance-based methods (fpc::clusterboot), and a
#     posterior-based bootstrap Adjusted Rand Index for the model-based
#     GMM/LPA, since GMM classifications are probabilistic rather than
#     assigned by a fixed distance rule.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
assess_distance_quality <- function(labels, method_label, k) {
  n <- length(labels)
  size_tab <- table(labels) / n * 100
  min_size <- min(size_tab)

  eta_sq <- sapply(colnames(continuous_scaled), function(v) {
    a <- summary(aov(continuous_scaled[, v] ~ as.factor(labels)))
    a[[1]]["as.factor(labels)", "Sum Sq"] / sum(a[[1]][, "Sum Sq"])
  })
  distinctiveness <- mean(eta_sq)

  sil <- mean(cluster::silhouette(labels, dist_mat)[, 3])

  set.seed(1526)
  if (method_label == "Ward's hierarchical") {
    cb <- fpc::clusterboot(continuous_scaled, B = STABILITY_B_DIST,
                            clustermethod = fpc::hclustCBI, k = k,
                            method = "ward.D2", count = FALSE)
  } else {
    cb <- fpc::clusterboot(continuous_scaled, B = STABILITY_B_DIST,
                            clustermethod = fpc::kmeansCBI, k = k,
                            count = FALSE)
  }
  stability <- mean(cb$bootmean)

  centroids <- sapply(colnames(continuous_scaled), function(v) {
    tapply(continuous_scaled[, v], labels, mean)
  })
  n_defining <- rowSums(abs(centroids) >= DEFINING_NEED_Z)
  interpretability <- mean(n_defining)
  pct_uninterpretable <- mean(n_defining == 0) * 100

  stopifnot(
    "distinctiveness must be scalar" = length(distinctiveness) == 1,
    "sil must be scalar" = length(sil) == 1,
    "stability must be scalar" = length(stability) == 1,
    "interpretability must be scalar" = length(interpretability) == 1,
    "pct_uninterpretable must be scalar" = length(pct_uninterpretable) == 1
  )

  tibble(
    method = method_label, k = k, n_used = n,
    min_segment_pct = round(min_size, 1),
    any_segment_below_min = min_size < MIN_VIABLE_SEGMENT_PCT,
    distinctiveness_eta_sq = round(distinctiveness, 3),
    mean_silhouette = round(sil, 3),
    entropy = NA_real_,
    stability_index = round(stability, 3),
    mean_defining_needs = round(interpretability, 2),
    pct_segments_uninterpretable = round(pct_uninterpretable, 1)
  )
}

# --- GMM/LPA quality assessment --------------------------------------------
assess_gmm_quality <- function(fit, k) {
  n <- fit$n
  size_tab <- table(fit$classification) / n * 100
  min_size <- min(size_tab)
  ent <- calc_entropy(fit$z)

  centroids <- t(fit$parameters$mean)
  n_defining <- rowSums(abs(centroids) >= DEFINING_NEED_Z)
  interpretability <- mean(n_defining)
  pct_uninterpretable <- mean(n_defining == 0) * 100

  set.seed(1526)
  orig_class <- fit$classification
  boot_ari <- replicate(STABILITY_B_GMM, {
    tryCatch({
      idx <- sample(seq_len(nrow(continuous_scaled)), replace = TRUE)
      boot_fit <- mclust::Mclust(continuous_scaled[idx, ], G = k)
      pred <- predict(boot_fit, newdata = continuous_scaled)
      mclust::adjustedRandIndex(orig_class, pred$classification)
    }, error = function(e) NA_real_)
  })
  stability <- mean(boot_ari, na.rm = TRUE)

  stopifnot(
    "ent must be scalar" = length(ent) == 1,
    "stability must be scalar" = length(stability) == 1,
    "interpretability must be scalar" = length(interpretability) == 1,
    "pct_uninterpretable must be scalar" = length(pct_uninterpretable) == 1
  )

  tibble(
    method = "GMM/LPA", k = k, n_used = n,
    min_segment_pct = round(min_size, 1),
    any_segment_below_min = min_size < MIN_VIABLE_SEGMENT_PCT,
    distinctiveness_eta_sq = NA_real_,
    mean_silhouette = NA_real_,
    entropy = round(ent, 3),
    stability_index = round(stability, 3),
    mean_defining_needs = round(interpretability, 2),
    pct_segments_uninterpretable = round(pct_uninterpretable, 1)
  )
}

quality_table <- bind_rows(
  purrr::map2_dfr(SHORTLIST_K, candidate_dist, function(k, cand) {
    assess_distance_quality(cand$ward, "Ward's hierarchical", k)
  }),
  purrr::map2_dfr(SHORTLIST_K, candidate_dist, function(k, cand) {
    assess_distance_quality(cand$kmeans, "K-means (confirmatory)", k)
  }),
  purrr::map2_dfr(SHORTLIST_K, candidate_gmm, function(k, fit) {
    assess_gmm_quality(fit, k)
  })
)

# Composite quality score (0-1, higher = better): an unweighted average of
# four min-max-normalised sub-scores (size adequacy, distinctiveness/
# entropy, stability, interpretability). This is a transparent SHORTLISTING
# heuristic to narrow nine candidates down for close reading -- not a
# statistical test -- the final choice in Section 13 still requires the
# analyst's substantive judgement (WBS brief: "recommend the final
# segmentation model with rationale").
norm01 <- function(x) {
  x[is.na(x)] <- min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (diff(range(x)) == 0) return(rep(1, length(x)))
  (x - min(x)) / diff(range(x))
}
quality_table <- quality_table %>%
  mutate(
    size_score = norm01(pmin(min_segment_pct, 15)),
    interpretability_score = norm01(mean_defining_needs)
  )
# size_score and interpretability_score are deliberately left normalised
# GLOBALLY across all 9 candidates -- not an oversight. min_segment_pct and
# mean_defining_needs are computed via the IDENTICAL formula for every
# method (the same "% of respondents in the smallest segment"; the same
# count of factors clearing |z| >= DEFINING_NEED_Z), so there is no
# different-statistics scale-mixing risk of the kind separation_score had.
# stability_score does NOT get the same pass -- see the fix below.

# FIXED (2026-08-02, after first real knit-through): separation is measured
# on two DIFFERENT statistics depending on method family -- eta-squared
# (variance explained by cluster) for the two distance-based methods, vs.
# posterior entropy (classification clarity) for GMM/LPA. The original
# implementation min-max-normalised both together on ONE shared scale via
# `norm01(ifelse(method == "GMM/LPA", entropy, distinctiveness_eta_sq))`.
# On the first real run, entropy (0.73-0.78 across all 3 GMM candidates)
# happened to sit on a numerically higher range than eta-squared
# (0.40-0.55 across all 6 distance-based candidates) -- so EVERY GMM
# candidate scored near 1.0 and EVERY Ward's/K-means candidate scored near
# 0 on this sub-score, regardless of which candidates were actually more
# separated. That artifact was the dominant reason GMM/LPA k=4 (composite
# 0.852) beat K-means k=4 (composite 0.544, despite K-means k=4 having far
# higher bootstrap stability: 0.833 vs 0.549) in that run. Fixed by
# normalising each family against its OWN candidates only -- eta-squared is
# still directly comparable BETWEEN Ward's and K-means (same statistic,
# same data), just no longer forced onto the same scale as GMM's entropy.
is_gmm <- quality_table$method == "GMM/LPA"
quality_table$separation_score <- NA_real_
quality_table$separation_score[is_gmm]  <- norm01(quality_table$entropy[is_gmm])
quality_table$separation_score[!is_gmm] <- norm01(quality_table$distinctiveness_eta_sq[!is_gmm])

# FIXED (2026-08-03): stability_score carried the same latent scale-mixing
# risk separation_score originally had, just less consequential so far.
# Ward's/K-means stability_index is a Jaccard bootstrap co-membership mean
# (fpc::clusterboot); GMM/LPA's is a posterior-classification bootstrap
# Adjusted Rand Index (Section 12, assess_gmm_quality). Both are
# conventionally read as "0 = unstable, 1 = perfectly stable", but they are
# different estimators with no guarantee of occupying the same numeric
# range on a given dataset -- exactly the reasoning that motivated splitting
# separation_score. Normalised per method family here for consistency.
quality_table$stability_score <- NA_real_
quality_table$stability_score[is_gmm]  <- norm01(quality_table$stability_index[is_gmm])
quality_table$stability_score[!is_gmm] <- norm01(quality_table$stability_index[!is_gmm])

quality_table <- quality_table %>%
  mutate(composite_quality = round((size_score + separation_score + stability_score +
                                       interpretability_score) / 4, 3))
cat("Segment quality assessment across all 9 candidate (method x k) solutions:\n")
print(quality_table %>% select(method, k, min_segment_pct, distinctiveness_eta_sq,
                                 entropy, stability_index, mean_defining_needs,
                                 composite_quality))

## FIGURE: composite quality score by method x k.
p_quality <- ggplot2::ggplot(quality_table,
                              ggplot2::aes(x = as.factor(k), y = composite_quality, fill = method)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = composite_quality),
                      position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Segment quality assessment: composite score by method x segment count",
                x = "Number of segments (k)", y = "Composite quality score (0-1)", fill = "Method") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_quality)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "quality_comparison.png"), p_quality, width = 9, height = 6)
```

TABLE: full segment quality assessment across all nine candidates.

```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
print(knitr::kable(quality_table %>%
                      select(method, k, min_segment_pct, distinctiveness_eta_sq, entropy,
                             stability_index, mean_defining_needs, composite_quality),
                    digits = 3, caption = "Segment quality assessment (9 candidates)"))
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 12b. ALL-CANDIDATES PROFILE COMPARISON (added on user request, 2026-08-06)
#      The Section 13 recommendation only ever plots ONE profile heatmap --
#      the programmatic winner's. On reviewing the recommended K-means k=4
#      solution, 3 of its 4 segments looked visually "flat" (most |z| under
#      0.8) next to one sharply differentiated segment. Section 3's
#      correlation heatmap explains why structurally: 6 of the 8 clustering
#      inputs are moderately-to-strongly positively intercorrelated (a
#      dominant general need-intensity axis), while NeedFA3 ("provider needs
#      a deep understanding of our business" + 4 related relationship/
#      account-management items) ran strongly negative against that axis in
#      the original (pre-2026-08-22) run. UPDATED 2026-08-22: C5c's raw items
#      were found to be reverse-coded and fixed (see 02c Section 3.2). Since
#      NeedFA3 is now the mirror image of before, its correlation with every
#      other factor flips sign too (corr(-X,Y) = -corr(X,Y)) -- it now runs
#      strongly POSITIVE against the dominant axis instead, i.e. it no longer
#      acts as a countervailing dimension (sign flip is mathematically
#      certain; exact new correlation magnitude not independently re-pulled
#      from a printed matrix here). If anything this makes segments even
#      more likely to differ along one dominant tilt rather than in sharply
#      distinct shapes, so eta-squared of 0.42 (K-means k=4) still reflects
#      that honestly rather than indicating weak clustering.
#      This section makes that trade-off visually inspectable rather than
#      asserted: every one of the 9 shortlisted candidates gets its own
#      profile panel, labelled with its own composite_quality score, so
#      "does k=5/6 actually look meaningfully more differentiated" can be
#      judged directly against the quality/stability cost already quantified
#      in Section 12's table, instead of guessed at from the single winner.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_candidate_profile <- function(labels, method_label, k) {
  centroids <- sapply(colnames(continuous_scaled), function(v) {
    tapply(continuous_scaled[, v], labels, mean)
  })
  as.data.frame(centroids) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("segment") %>%
    mutate(method = method_label, k = k)
}

all_candidate_profiles <- bind_rows(
  purrr::map2_dfr(SHORTLIST_K, candidate_dist, function(k, cand) {
    build_candidate_profile(cand$ward, "Ward's hierarchical", k)
  }),
  purrr::map2_dfr(SHORTLIST_K, candidate_dist, function(k, cand) {
    build_candidate_profile(cand$kmeans, "K-means (confirmatory)", k)
  }),
  purrr::map2_dfr(SHORTLIST_K, candidate_gmm, function(k, fit) {
    build_candidate_profile(fit$classification, "GMM/LPA", k)
  })
)

# Panel order/labels follow quality_table's own row order (method blocks of
# k=4,5,6 each) and fold in each candidate's composite_quality score
# directly into the facet strip, so distinctiveness and quality/stability
# can be read side by side rather than cross-referenced against a separate
# table.
# BUGFIX (caught on visual QA of the first re-knit): the original panel
# labels ("Ward's hierarchical, k=4  (composite=0.377)", ~44 characters)
# were wider than facet_wrap allocates per strip at this plot size and got
# clipped on BOTH edges -- "Ward's" lost its leading W, composite values
# were cut off entirely for the K-means row. ggplot doesn't auto-wrap or
# auto-shrink strip text, so the fix is to shorten the source strings, not
# the theme: abbreviate the method name and split the k/quality onto a
# second line via "\n" so each line only needs to fit ~12 characters.
method_abbrev <- c("Ward's hierarchical" = "Ward's", "K-means (confirmatory)" = "K-means",
                    "GMM/LPA" = "GMM/LPA")
panel_order <- paste0(quality_table$method, ", k=", quality_table$k)
panel_lookup <- setNames(
  paste0(method_abbrev[quality_table$method], ", k=", quality_table$k,
         "\n(q=", quality_table$composite_quality, ")"),
  panel_order
)
all_candidate_profiles_long <- all_candidate_profiles %>%
  mutate(panel_key = paste0(method, ", k=", k),
         panel = factor(panel_lookup[panel_key], levels = unname(panel_lookup[panel_order]))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::all_of(num_cols), names_to = "need", values_to = "z")

p_all_candidates <- ggplot2::ggplot(all_candidate_profiles_long,
                                     ggplot2::aes(x = need, y = segment, fill = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%+.1f", z)), size = 2.2) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0,
                                  name = "z-score") +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 3) +
  # BUGFIX: this subtitle (~170 characters) was also clipped at the plot
  # edge -- shortened to fit; "q" is defined inline since the full
  # composite_quality name no longer appears in the (now-abbreviated)
  # panel titles either.
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Segment profiles across all 9 shortlisted candidates",
                subtitle = "q = composite_quality (Section 12) -- a higher q already prices in the stability cost of a sharper split",
                x = NULL, y = "Segment") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
                 strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 7.5))
print(p_all_candidates)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "all_candidates_profile_comparison.png"), p_all_candidates,
                 width = 15, height = 11)
cat("\nAll 9 candidate profiles saved to all_candidates_profile_comparison.png -- use this to",
    "judge whether a higher-k solution's extra distinctiveness is worth its lower composite_quality",
    "and stability_index (see Section 12's table) before overriding the Section 13 recommendation.\n")
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. RECOMMENDED SEGMENTATION MODEL -- FINAL SELECTION + PROFILES
#     ("Recommend the final segmentation model with rationale and
#     limitations" -- WBS Workstream 2 brief)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Selection rule: highest composite_quality among candidates with NO segment
# below the minimum viable size; ties broken by stability. This programmatic
# pick is a starting point for the analyst to confirm or override once the
# profiles below are reviewed -- not a black box (see Section 15).
viable <- quality_table %>% filter(!any_segment_below_min)
if (nrow(viable) == 0) {
  cat("\nWARNING: every candidate has at least one segment below",
      MIN_VIABLE_SEGMENT_PCT, "% -- selecting on composite_quality alone; ",
      "review segment sizes before treating this as final.\n")
  viable <- quality_table
}
best <- viable %>% arrange(desc(composite_quality), desc(stability_index)) %>% slice(1)
cat("\nRECOMMENDED SOLUTION (programmatic shortlist pick -- confirm before finalising):\n")
print(best)

REC_METHOD <- best$method
REC_K      <- best$k

if (REC_METHOD == "GMM/LPA") {
  rec_fit <- candidate_gmm[[paste0("k", REC_K)]]
  rec_labels_df <- tibble(uuid = continuous_input$uuid, segment = rec_fit$classification)
  rec_profile <- as.data.frame(t(rec_fit$parameters$mean)) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("segment")
} else {
  cand <- candidate_dist[[paste0("k", REC_K)]]
  rec_labels <- if (REC_METHOD == "Ward's hierarchical") cand$ward else cand$kmeans
  rec_labels_df <- tibble(uuid = continuous_input$uuid, segment = rec_labels)
  rec_profile <- as.data.frame(sapply(colnames(continuous_scaled), function(v) {
    tapply(continuous_scaled[, v], rec_labels, mean)
  })) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("segment")
}

rec_size <- rec_labels_df %>% count(segment) %>%
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))
cat("\nRecommended segmentation -- segment sizes:\n"); print(rec_size)

## FIGURE: recommended segmentation -- segment size chart.
p_rec_size <- ggplot2::ggplot(rec_size, ggplot2::aes(x = as.factor(segment), y = pct)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "darkorange3") +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(pct, "%")), vjust = -0.3) +
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = MIN_VIABLE_SEGMENT_PCT, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("Recommended segmentation (", REC_METHOD, ", k = ", REC_K, "): segment sizes"),
                subtitle = "Dashed line = minimum viable segment size",
                x = "Segment", y = "% of respondents") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_rec_size)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "recommended_segment_sizes.png"), p_rec_size, width = 8, height = 5)

## FIGURE: recommended segmentation -- need profile.
rec_profile_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(rec_profile, cols = -segment, names_to = "need", values_to = "z")
p_rec_profile <- ggplot2::ggplot(rec_profile_long,
                                  ggplot2::aes(x = need, y = as.factor(segment), fill = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "steelblue4", mid = "white", high = "firebrick3", midpoint = 0) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("Recommended segmentation (", REC_METHOD, "): need profile (z-scores)"),
                x = "Need factor", y = "Segment", fill = "z-score") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_rec_profile)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "recommended_profile.png"), p_rec_profile, width = 9, height = 5)

## FIGURE: recommended segmentation on the same PCA projection of the need
## space used in Section 5, so it can be visually compared to the
## unconstrained K-means solution shown there.
pca_rec_df <- tibble(uuid = rownames(continuous_scaled),
                      PC1 = pca_needs$x[, 1], PC2 = pca_needs$x[, 2]) %>%
  inner_join(rec_labels_df %>% mutate(segment = as.factor(segment)), by = "uuid")
p_rec_pca <- ggplot2::ggplot(pca_rec_df, ggplot2::aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = segment)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1.6) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = paste0("Recommended segmentation (", REC_METHOD, ", k = ", REC_K, ") -- PCA projection"),
                x = "PC1", y = "PC2", colour = "Segment") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_rec_pca)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "recommended_pca_scatter.png"), p_rec_pca, width = 8, height = 6)

## FIGURE: recommended segmentation vs firmographics (S2/S3/S4/D3) -- the
## commercially actionable "who is in each segment" picture.
rec_firmo <- rec_labels_df %>% mutate(segment = as.factor(segment)) %>% left_join(firmo, by = "uuid")

p_rec_sector <- ggplot2::ggplot(rec_firmo %>% filter(!is.na(S4)),
                                 ggplot2::aes(x = segment, fill = S4)) +
  ggplot2::geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Recommended segmentation: sector composition (S4)",
                x = "Segment", y = "% of segment", fill = "Sector") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7))
print(p_rec_sector)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "recommended_sector_composition.png"), p_rec_sector, width = 9, height = 6)

p_rec_employees <- ggplot2::ggplot(rec_firmo %>% filter(!is.na(S2), S2 > 0),
                                    ggplot2::aes(x = segment, y = S2)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(fill = "lightsteelblue3") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Recommended segmentation: employee count (S2, log scale)",
                x = "Segment", y = "Employees (log10 scale)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_rec_employees)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "recommended_employees_boxplot.png"), p_rec_employees, width = 8, height = 5)
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13b. HIGH-LEVEL SEGMENT PROFILING (business-facing narrative + charts)
#     Section 13's outputs are statistically complete but not something a
#     client account team will read directly (factor z-scores, p-values). This
#     section translates the recommended solution into named personas, a
#     compact need-factor heatmap with plain-English factor labels, and a
#     firmographic company-size comparison -- per the WBS brief's "equal
#     emphasis on commercial applicability" mandate.
#
#     IMPORTANT -- FACTOR_THEMES and SEGMENT_THEMES below are ANALYST-
#     ASSIGNED labels (2026-08-02), not computed from the data. They were
#     written by reading the Reduction Stage's "FA Loadings (selected k)"
#     top items per factor (FA1=MR4, FA2=MR5, FA3=MR3, FA4=MR1, FA5=MR2 in
#     that stage's k=5 solution) and this script's Segment Profile +
#     firmographic breakdown for the GMM/LPA k=4 recommended solution. Both
#     guards below (`factor_labels_valid`, `segment_labels_valid`) check
#     the CURRENT knit's inputs still match what these labels were written
#     for; if the Reduction Stage's factor count/order changes, or a
#     different method/k becomes the recommended solution, this section
#     automatically falls back to generic FA1/FA2/... and "Segment 1/2/..."
#     labels instead of silently mislabelling a different solution. If that
#     happens, re-derive both lookups by re-reading the new Segment Profile
#     and firmographic tables before re-enabling the custom labels.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): FACTOR_THEMES was previously left empty
# for every SCORE_SET including "hierarchical", so the profiling heatmap and
# the Segment Defining Variables sheet showed raw score codes (e.g.
# "F3_Factor1") rather than a human-readable theme -- and the FA-specific
# labels this section used to support required hand-deriving and manually
# pasting a new lookup every time the recommended solution changed, exactly
# the kind of label that goes stale silently (see git history / prior
# comment). Auto-derive a short, self-updating theme label for each combined
# score instead, from its own top-loading raw item in
# `reduction_obj$score_item_map` (guaranteed present for this script -- see
# Section 1's stopifnot) -- no manual re-derivation step required on future
# re-knits, and it can never mismatch the currently-loaded solution the way a
# hard-coded vector could.
auto_factor_theme <- function(sc) {
  if (!"score_item_map" %in% names(reduction_obj)) return(sc)
  rows <- reduction_obj$score_item_map[reduction_obj$score_item_map$score_col == sc, ]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(sc)
  top_label <- rows$item_label[which.max(abs(rows$loading))]
  # BUGFIX (caught on visual QA of the first re-knit after this feature was
  # added): some item labels are long ("Satellite / Non-Terrestrial Network
  # connectivity", "Network personalisation (NaaS with APIs)") -- 8 of these
  # side by side on one plot's x-axis overlapped into unreadable garbled text.
  # Truncated here to a short phrase; kept single-line since this label is
  # also used verbatim in the Segment Defining Variables xlsx export
  # (Section 13c) -- the plot-only line-wrapped version is built separately,
  # just below the profiling heatmap code, so the xlsx cell stays clean.
  short_label <- if (nchar(top_label) > 22) paste0(substr(top_label, 1, 21), "…") else top_label
  paste0(sc, " (", short_label, ")")
}
FACTOR_THEMES <- setNames(vapply(num_cols, auto_factor_theme, character(1)), num_cols)
factor_labels_valid <- length(FACTOR_THEMES) > 0 && setequal(names(FACTOR_THEMES), num_cols)

# ADDED (2026-08-10, critical-analysis pass): these four names/one-line
# framings are analyst-authored (the underlying data pattern can be
# auto-derived -- see seg_defining below -- but naming/commercial framing
# genuinely requires judgement, per the note above). Written by reading
# THIS run's live Segment Profile (Section 13) z-scores and the
# firmographic breakdown (median employees/sites by segment, joined from
# the raw firmographic file) for the CURRENT recommended solution
# (K-means (confirmatory), k = 4) -- not carried over from an older run,
# unlike the GMM/LPA-era labels this replaced.
SEGMENT_THEMES <- c(
  "1" = "Tech-Forward Enterprises",
  "2" = "Value-Driven Operators",
  "3" = "Minimal-Needs Micro Accounts",
  "4" = "Modest-Expectation Larger Accounts"
)
# Re-uses the SAME defensive pattern as factor_labels_valid above: only
# treat these labels as valid if the CURRENT run's recommended
# method/k/segment-count still matches what they were written for. If a
# future re-knit changes the recommendation (different method, different
# k, or a different number of segments than SEGMENT_THEMES has names for),
# this automatically flips back to FALSE and the NOTE/fallback logic below
# fires -- exactly the staleness guard the removed persona_desc block
# lacked.
segment_labels_valid <- identical(REC_METHOD, "K-means (confirmatory)") &&
  isTRUE(REC_K == 4) &&
  setequal(names(SEGMENT_THEMES), as.character(sort(unique(rec_profile$segment))))

if (!factor_labels_valid) {
  cat("NOTE: FACTOR_THEMES labels do not match the current factor set (",
      paste(num_cols, collapse = ", "), ") -- falling back to generic factor",
      "labels in the profiling charts below. Re-derive FACTOR_THEMES from",
      "the Reduction Stage's current 'FA Loadings (selected k)' sheet.\n")
}
if (!segment_labels_valid) {
  cat("NOTE: SEGMENT_THEMES labels were written for the GMM/LPA k=4 solution",
      "specifically; the current recommended solution is", REC_METHOD, "k =",
      REC_K, "-- falling back to generic 'Segment N' labels below. Re-derive",
      "SEGMENT_THEMES by re-reading the Segment Profile/firmographic tables",
      "for this solution.\n")
}

factor_label_lookup <- if (factor_labels_valid) FACTOR_THEMES else setNames(num_cols, num_cols)
segment_label_lookup <- function(seg) {
  seg_chr <- as.character(seg)
  if (segment_labels_valid && seg_chr %in% names(SEGMENT_THEMES)) {
    paste0("Segment ", seg_chr, ": ", SEGMENT_THEMES[[seg_chr]])
  } else {
    paste0("Segment ", seg_chr)
  }
}

## FIGURE: need-factor heatmap with plain-English factor labels -- a more
## reader-friendly companion to the technical `p_rec_profile` heatmap
## produced in Section 13.
# BUGFIX: the auto-derived FACTOR_THEMES labels (e.g. "F3_Factor1 (Network
# personalisation (NaaS wit…))") are too long to sit side-by-side as x-axis
# text without overlapping -- confirmed on visual QA of the first re-knit.
# Line-wrapping the item-label part (below) fixed most of it, but
# "ProviderPerception_Factor1" alone is 27 characters -- long enough that
# its wrapped label still overlapped its neighbour on the second re-knit's
# visual QA. Re-derive the plot label from scratch (rather than
# post-processing the xlsx-facing string) so the SCORE-CODE portion can
# also be shortened for display, in addition to the item-label wrap --
# `factor_label_lookup`/`FACTOR_THEMES` themselves are untouched and stay
# full-length/single-line for the xlsx export.
auto_factor_theme_plot <- function(sc) {
  short_sc <- if (nchar(sc) > 12) paste0(substr(sc, 1, 11), "…") else sc
  if (!"score_item_map" %in% names(reduction_obj)) return(short_sc)
  rows <- reduction_obj$score_item_map[reduction_obj$score_item_map$score_col == sc, ]
  if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(short_sc)
  top_label <- rows$item_label[which.max(abs(rows$loading))]
  short_label <- if (nchar(top_label) > 22) paste0(substr(top_label, 1, 21), "…") else top_label
  paste0(short_sc, "\n(", short_label, ")")
}
plot_factor_label_lookup <- setNames(vapply(num_cols, auto_factor_theme_plot, character(1)), num_cols)
profile_theme_df <- rec_profile
matched_cols <- names(profile_theme_df) %in% names(plot_factor_label_lookup)
names(profile_theme_df)[matched_cols] <- plot_factor_label_lookup[names(profile_theme_df)[matched_cols]]
profile_theme_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(profile_theme_df, cols = -segment, names_to = "need", values_to = "z")
seg_levels <- sapply(sort(unique(profile_theme_df$segment)), segment_label_lookup)
profile_theme_long$segment_label <- factor(sapply(profile_theme_long$segment, segment_label_lookup), levels = seg_levels)

# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): this subtitle was previously a
# hard-coded caption about a specific factor ("BYOD/Cloud Storage",
# alpha = -0.01) left over from an older FA-specific run of this section --
# it no longer describes anything in this hierarchical score set, and would
# now render on every knit since factor_labels_valid is TRUE above (it used
# to gate this exact string). Replaced with a caption built from THIS run's
# actual `reduction_obj$score_reliability` flags, so it can never show a
# factor/alpha pair that isn't part of the current run.
unreliable_theme_note <- {
  ur <- reduction_obj$score_reliability$score_col[reduction_obj$score_reliability$reliable %in% FALSE]
  if (length(ur) == 0) NULL else paste0("*", paste(ur, collapse = ", "),
    " failed the Stage 1 reliability bar (Cronbach's alpha < 0.70) -- treat as directional only")
}
p_theme_heat <- ggplot2::ggplot(profile_theme_long, ggplot2::aes(x = need, y = segment_label, fill = z)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%+.2f", z),
                                    colour = abs(z) > 0.75), fontface = "bold", size = 3.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "black")) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "white", high = "#B2182B", midpoint = 0,
                                  limits = c(-1.5, 1.5), name = "Standardised\nneed score (z)") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "What defines each segment: need-factor profile",
                subtitle = unreliable_theme_note,
                x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7.5, angle = 20, hjust = 0.9, vjust = 1),
                 plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8, face = "italic", colour = "grey40"))
print(p_theme_heat)
# BUGFIX: widened from 10" to 13" (auto-derived labels are longer than the
# generic score codes this plot was originally sized for -- see
# auto_factor_theme above) so the two-line "code\n(short item)" labels have
# room to render without overlapping.
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "profiling_need_heatmap.png"), p_theme_heat, width = 13, height = 5.5)

## FIGURE: segment sizes with named-persona legend.
rec_size_theme <- rec_size
rec_size_theme$segment_label <- factor(sapply(rec_size_theme$segment, segment_label_lookup), levels = seg_levels)
p_size_theme <- ggplot2::ggplot(rec_size_theme, ggplot2::aes(x = factor(segment), y = pct, fill = segment_label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = paste0(pct, "%\n(n=", n, ")")), vjust = -0.15, fontface = "bold", size = 3.4) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(rec_size_theme$pct) * 1.25)) +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Segment sizes", x = "Segment", y = "% of respondents", fill = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 1))
print(p_size_theme)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "profiling_segment_sizes.png"), p_size_theme, width = 8, height = 5.5)

## FIGURE: company size by segment (median employees + median sites) -- the
## sharpest firmographic differentiator found during profiling. Sector
## composition (S4) was also checked and found to be broadly flat across
## segments, so it is not repeated here
## as a headline chart -- see `recommended_sector_composition.png`
## (Section 13) for the full breakdown if needed.
firmo_size_summary <- rec_firmo %>%
  group_by(segment) %>%
  summarise(median_employees = median(S2, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_sites = median(S3, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
firmo_size_summary$segment_label <- factor(sapply(firmo_size_summary$segment, segment_label_lookup), levels = seg_levels)

p_profiling_emp <- ggplot2::ggplot(firmo_size_summary, ggplot2::aes(x = factor(segment), y = median_employees, fill = segment_label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = round(median_employees)), vjust = -0.3, fontface = "bold") +
  ggplot2::scale_y_log10() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Company size by segment", x = "Segment", y = "Median employees (log scale)", fill = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(ncol = 1))
print(p_profiling_emp)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "profiling_company_size.png"), p_profiling_emp, width = 7.5, height = 5.5)

p_profiling_sites <- ggplot2::ggplot(firmo_size_summary, ggplot2::aes(x = factor(segment), y = median_sites, fill = segment_label)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = median_sites), vjust = -0.3, fontface = "bold") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Number of sites by segment", x = "Segment", y = "Median number of sites") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
print(p_profiling_sites)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "profiling_site_count.png"), p_profiling_sites, width = 6.5, height = 5)

## Named, EXPORT-ONLY copies of the segment size/profile/assignment tables
## (persona name added as a column) for the xlsx workbook in Section 16.
## Kept SEPARATE from rec_labels_df itself, because rec_labels_df is also
## the CART TRAINING TARGET in Section 14 -- joining a segment_persona
## column into it there would hand the tree a column that is just a
## renamed copy of the outcome, corrupting the "rules" it learns.
rec_size_named      <- rec_size %>% mutate(segment_persona = sapply(segment, segment_label_lookup), .after = segment)
rec_profile_named   <- rec_profile %>% mutate(segment_persona = sapply(segment, segment_label_lookup), .after = segment)
rec_labels_df_named <- rec_labels_df %>% mutate(segment_persona = sapply(segment, segment_label_lookup), .after = segment)

## ------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Variable-level segment mapping: which RAW SURVEY VARIABLES (named
## exactly as in the source data file -- see ../../../data/README.md,
## e.g. "C5c_1r1", "F9ar6") define each segment's defining need factors.
## Recomputed here directly from `reduction_obj$fa_res$loadings` -- NOT
## hard-coded or re-read from a separately-saved lookup -- using the SAME
## loading-cutoff assignment rule the Reduction Stage itself used
## (LOADING_CUTOFF = 0.40), so this mapping automatically stays in sync
## with whichever fa_res is currently loaded from reduction_stage_objects.rds
## rather than silently drifting out of date if that script is re-run with
## a different item set or factor solution.
## ------------------------------------------------------------------------
LOADING_CUTOFF_PROFILING <- 0.40   # must match LOADING_CUTOFF in 02c_Reduction_Stage_WS1Needs.Rmd
fa_loadings_mat <- unclass(reduction_obj$fa_res$loadings)
variable_mapping_valid <- identical(SCORE_SET, "fa") && ncol(fa_loadings_mat) == length(num_cols)

# NEW (robustness-improvement pass, 2026-08-05): the hierarchical equivalent
# of variable_mapping_valid above. This variant never has SCORE_SET == "fa"
# (see Section 0), so the FA-specific branch above is always FALSE here --
# this flag gates an INDEPENDENT branch below that builds the same
# "Segment Defining Variables" output from `reduction_obj$score_item_map`
# (built in 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd's "score-traceability"
# chunk by reconciling all FOUR of Stage 1's separate loadings matrices),
# rather than leaving the mapping permanently inert for this variant.
hierarchical_defining_vars_valid <- identical(SCORE_SET, "hierarchical") &&
  all(c("score_item_map", "score_reliability") %in% names(reduction_obj))

# Per-factor Cronbach's alpha / reliability flag, keyed to FA1..FA5 by
# matching `factor_reliability$factor` (MR-named, e.g. "MR4") against
# fa_loadings_mat's own column names -- POSITIONAL, not a hard-coded
# MR->FA mapping, so it stays correct even if the Reduction Stage's factor
# order/naming changes on a future re-run. A factor missing from
# factor_reliability (e.g. it had fewer than 2 assigned items) or the
# whole component being absent both degrade to NA rather than erroring.
if (has_factor_reliability) {
  rel_idx <- match(colnames(fa_loadings_mat), reduction_obj$factor_reliability$factor)
  factor_alpha_lookup    <- setNames(reduction_obj$factor_reliability$cronbach_alpha[rel_idx], num_cols)
  factor_reliable_lookup <- setNames(reduction_obj$factor_reliability$reliable[rel_idx], num_cols)
} else {
  factor_alpha_lookup    <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(num_cols)), num_cols)
  factor_reliable_lookup <- setNames(rep(NA, length(num_cols)), num_cols)
}

if (variable_mapping_valid) {
  assign_item_to_factor <- function(row) {
    best <- which.max(abs(row))
    if (abs(row[best]) >= LOADING_CUTOFF_PROFILING) num_cols[best] else NA_character_
  }
  item_factor_map <- apply(fa_loadings_mat, 1, assign_item_to_factor)
  factor_variable_list <- setNames(
    lapply(num_cols, function(fa) names(item_factor_map)[!is.na(item_factor_map) & item_factor_map == fa]),
    num_cols
  )

  segment_defining_vars <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(rec_profile)), function(i) {
    seg    <- as.character(rec_profile$segment[i])
    z_vals <- unlist(rec_profile[i, num_cols])
    defining_factors <- num_cols[abs(z_vals) >= DEFINING_NEED_Z]
    purrr::map_dfr(defining_factors, function(fa) {
      vars <- factor_variable_list[[fa]]
      if (length(vars) == 0) return(NULL)
      # Descriptive questionnaire text for each variable, e.g. "F1r2" ->
      # "Sovereign cloud" -- looked up from the Reduction Stage's own
      # `all_blocks` labels (saved as `item_labels` in the RDS), so the
      # wording always matches that script's xlsx output exactly. Falls
      # back to the raw code itself if `item_labels` wasn't available.
      var_labels <- if (has_item_labels) {
        looked_up <- unname(reduction_obj$item_labels[vars])
        ifelse(is.na(looked_up), vars, looked_up)
      } else {
        vars
      }
      tibble::tibble(
        segment         = seg,
        segment_persona = segment_label_lookup(seg),
        factor          = fa,
        factor_theme    = if (factor_labels_valid) trimws(gsub("\n", " ", FACTOR_THEMES[[fa]])) else fa,
        source_block    = NA_character_,
        need_direction  = ifelse(z_vals[[fa]] > 0, "Above average", "Below average"),
        z_score         = round(z_vals[[fa]], 3),
        variable        = vars,
        item_label      = var_labels,
        loading         = round(fa_loadings_mat[vars, match(fa, num_cols)], 3),
        factor_alpha    = unname(factor_alpha_lookup[fa]),
        factor_reliable = unname(factor_reliable_lookup[fa])
      )
    })
  })
  # `%in%` treats NA safely here (NA %in% FALSE is FALSE, not NA), so this
  # only counts rows genuinely flagged unreliable, not missing-reliability rows.
  n_unreliable_rows <- sum(segment_defining_vars$factor_reliable %in% FALSE)
  cat("Variable-level segment mapping: ", nrow(segment_defining_vars),
      "(segment x defining-factor x raw-variable) rows across",
      length(unique(segment_defining_vars$segment)), "segments (",
      n_unreliable_rows, "rows belong to a factor flagged unreliable, factor_reliable = FALSE ).\n")
} else if (hierarchical_defining_vars_valid) {
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # HIERARCHICAL VARIANT (02d): reconciles Stage 1's FOUR separate loadings
  # matrices (45-item pool's 5 FA factors + F1's + F3's + ProviderPerception's
  # own within-block factors) via `reduction_obj$score_item_map` -- built in
  # 02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd's "score-traceability" chunk,
  # exactly so this mapping would not have to stay permanently inert for
  # this variant (see that chunk's header for how it was built). Each row
  # here is one (segment x defining-score x raw-variable) combination,
  # carrying that score's Stage 1 reliability verdict (factor_alpha/
  # factor_reliable) AND which of the four Stage 1 blocks it came from
  # (source_block) -- so a reader can immediately see, e.g., that a
  # segment's F3_Factor1 defining variable rests on an alpha = 0.263,
  # NOT-reliable factor, not just that F3r3/F3r13 happen to be listed.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  segment_defining_vars <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(rec_profile)), function(i) {
    seg    <- as.character(rec_profile$segment[i])
    z_vals <- unlist(rec_profile[i, num_cols])
    defining_scores <- num_cols[abs(z_vals) >= DEFINING_NEED_Z]
    purrr::map_dfr(defining_scores, function(sc) {
      rows <- reduction_obj$score_item_map[reduction_obj$score_item_map$score_col == sc, ]
      if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(NULL)
      tibble::tibble(
        segment         = seg,
        segment_persona = segment_label_lookup(seg),
        factor          = sc,
        factor_theme    = FACTOR_THEMES[[sc]],  # auto-derived label (Section 13b), self-updating
        source_block    = rows$source_block,
        need_direction  = ifelse(z_vals[[sc]] > 0, "Above average", "Below average"),
        z_score         = round(z_vals[[sc]], 3),
        variable        = rows$variable,
        item_label      = rows$item_label,
        loading         = rows$loading,
        factor_alpha    = rows$cronbach_alpha,
        factor_reliable = rows$reliable
      )
    })
  })
  n_unreliable_rows <- sum(segment_defining_vars$factor_reliable %in% FALSE)
  cat("Variable-level segment mapping (hierarchical, via score_item_map): ", nrow(segment_defining_vars),
      "(segment x defining-score x raw-variable) rows across",
      length(unique(segment_defining_vars$segment)), "segments (",
      n_unreliable_rows, "rows come from a score flagged unreliable, factor_reliable = FALSE -- see",
      "'Score Reliability Summary' and Section 13d's ablation check for how much this actually",
      "matters to the recommended segmentation).\n")
} else {
  cat("NOTE: variable-level segment mapping skipped -- neither the FA-specific path (SCORE_SET =",
      SCORE_SET, ") nor the hierarchical path (score_item_map/score_reliability present?",
      all(c("score_item_map", "score_reliability") %in% names(reduction_obj)),
      ") is valid for this run. Re-derive after re-knitting the Reduction Stage if this is unexpected.\n")
  segment_defining_vars <- tibble::tibble(
    segment = character(), segment_persona = character(), factor = character(),
    factor_theme = character(), source_block = character(), need_direction = character(),
    z_score = double(), factor_alpha = double(), factor_reliable = logical(),
    variable = character(), item_label = character(), loading = double()
  )
}
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 13d. ROBUSTNESS CHECK: SENSITIVITY OF THE RECOMMENDED SOLUTION TO
#      FLAGGED-UNRELIABLE SCORE INPUTS (ablation test)
#      Two of the eight combined scores (F3_Factor1, ProviderPerception_
#      Factor1 in the current run) failed the Stage 1 ALPHA_MIN reliability
#      bar (see 'Score Reliability Summary'). Rather than silently including
#      them and hoping they don't distort the recommended segmentation, or
#      silently dropping them and losing real item coverage, this section
#      does the empirical check directly: re-run the SAME recommended
#      method at the SAME k on a "core-only" subset that excludes every
#      flagged-unreliable score, and report how much the resulting
#      segmentation agrees with the main recommendation (Adjusted Rand
#      Index). This is the direct evidence for Browne's "are rival
#      explanations ruled out?" question applied to this pipeline's own
#      weakest link -- not an opinion about whether F3/ProviderPerception
#      "should" matter, a measurement of whether they DO.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
unreliable_scores <- if ("score_reliability" %in% names(reduction_obj)) {
  reduction_obj$score_reliability$score_col[reduction_obj$score_reliability$reliable %in% FALSE]
} else {
  character(0)
}
core_cols <- setdiff(num_cols, unreliable_scores)

cat("Score(s) flagged NOT reliable in Stage 1:",
    if (length(unreliable_scores) > 0) paste(unreliable_scores, collapse = ", ") else "(none)", "\n")

run_solution_on_subset <- function(cols, method, k) {
  scaled_subset <- continuous_scaled[, cols, drop = FALSE]
  if (method == "GMM/LPA") {
    fit <- mclust::Mclust(scaled_subset, G = k)
    fit$classification
  } else {
    hc_subset <- hclust(dist(scaled_subset, method = "euclidean"), method = HIER_METHOD)
    wc <- cutree(hc_subset, k = k)
    if (method == "Ward's hierarchical") {
      wc
    } else {
      wcent <- t(sapply(sort(unique(wc)), function(cl) colMeans(scaled_subset[wc == cl, , drop = FALSE])))
      kmeans(scaled_subset, centers = wcent, iter.max = 100)$cluster
    }
  }
}

if (length(unreliable_scores) == 0) {
  cat("No score column was flagged unreliable this run -- ablation check not applicable.\n")
  ablation_ari <- NA_real_
} else if (length(core_cols) < 2) {
  cat("WARNING: fewer than 2 score columns would remain after dropping the flagged-unreliable",
      "score(s) -- ablation check skipped (not enough dimensions to cluster on).\n")
  ablation_ari <- NA_real_
} else {
  cat("Re-running the recommended", REC_METHOD, "k =", REC_K, "solution on the remaining",
      length(core_cols), "score(s) only:", paste(core_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  set.seed(1526)
  core_labels <- run_solution_on_subset(core_cols, REC_METHOD, REC_K)
  ablation_ari <- mclust::adjustedRandIndex(rec_labels_df$segment, core_labels)
  core_size_pct <- round(table(core_labels) / length(core_labels) * 100, 1)

  cat("\nAdjusted Rand Index, full", length(num_cols), "-score recommended solution vs core-only (",
      length(core_cols), "-score) solution:", round(ablation_ari, 3), "\n")
  cat("Core-only segment sizes (%):\n"); print(core_size_pct)
  cat("Full-solution segment sizes (%) for comparison:\n"); print(rec_size$pct)

  if (ablation_ari >= 0.7) {
    cat("\nINTERPRETATION: high agreement -- the recommended segmentation is NOT materially",
        "dependent on the flagged-unreliable score(s); dropping them would not meaningfully",
        "change segment membership. The 80-item coverage these scores provide can be reported",
        "as additive, not load-bearing.\n")
  } else if (ablation_ari >= 0.4) {
    cat("\nINTERPRETATION: moderate agreement -- the flagged-unreliable score(s) have a real,",
        "partial influence on where segment boundaries fall. Report this ARI alongside the main",
        "result and treat the recommended solution's exact boundaries as somewhat sensitive to",
        "these scores' inclusion, even though the recommended method/k itself is unaffected.\n")
  } else {
    cat("\nINTERPRETATION: low agreement -- the recommended segmentation is materially dependent",
        "on the flagged-unreliable score(s). This is an important limitation to disclose:",
        "at least part of the segment structure is being driven by input(s) that failed the",
        "Stage 1 reliability bar, not just augmented by them.\n")
  }
}
```

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. CUSTOMER-TO-SEGMENT ASSIGNMENT RULES
#     ("Create clear rules for assigning customers to segments" -- WBS
#     Workstream 2 brief). A CART decision tree predicts the RECOMMENDED
#     segmentation's labels from the same factor scores used to build it,
#     producing simple, auditable if/then rules a client account team could
#     apply to a customer who was not in this survey sample.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
rule_data <- continuous_input %>%
  select(uuid, all_of(num_cols)) %>%
  inner_join(rec_labels_df, by = "uuid") %>%
  mutate(segment = as.factor(segment))

set.seed(1526)
train_idx  <- sample(seq_len(nrow(rule_data)), size = round(0.75 * nrow(rule_data)))
train_data <- rule_data[train_idx, ]
test_data  <- rule_data[-train_idx, ]

## cp is tuned by 10-fold cross-validation + the one-standard-error rule
## (Breiman et al., 1984) instead of being left at rpart's untuned 0.01
## default. Grow a deliberately permissive tree (cp near zero) so the
## cross-validated complexity path is fully visible, then prune back to
## the smallest tree within one standard error of the minimum
## cross-validated error. minbucket stays a fixed, data-proportional
## floor (2% of the training sample) rather than something to tune, since
## it exists to keep leaf-level rules legible for a client account team, not
## to optimise predictive fit.
full_tree <- rpart::rpart(
  segment ~ ., data = train_data %>% select(-uuid),
  method = "class",
  control = rpart::rpart.control(cp = 0.0001, minbucket = round(0.02 * nrow(train_data)), xval = 10)
)

cp_table        <- full_tree$cptable
min_xerror_row  <- which.min(cp_table[, "xerror"])
se_threshold    <- cp_table[min_xerror_row, "xerror"] + cp_table[min_xerror_row, "xstd"]
selected_row    <- min(which(cp_table[, "xerror"] <= se_threshold))
selected_cp     <- cp_table[selected_row, "CP"]

assignment_tree <- rpart::prune(full_tree, cp = selected_cp)

cat("CART complexity parameter selected via 10-fold CV + 1-SE rule: cp =",
    round(selected_cp, 4),
    "(vs. rpart's untuned default cp = 0.01; cross-validated error table below)\n")
print(cp_table)

## FIGURE: assignment-rule decision tree.
rpart.plot::rpart.plot(assignment_tree, type = 2, extra = 104, fallen.leaves = TRUE,
                        main = "Customer-to-Segment Assignment Rules")
dev.copy(png, file.path(output_dir, "segment_assignment_tree.png"), width = 1400, height = 900)
invisible(dev.off())

assignment_rules <- rpart.plot::rpart.rules(assignment_tree, style = "tall", cover = TRUE)
cat("Plain-English customer-to-segment assignment rules:\n")
print(assignment_rules)

pred_test <- predict(assignment_tree, newdata = test_data, type = "class")
tree_accuracy <- mean(pred_test == test_data$segment)
tree_kappa <- {
  tab <- table(pred_test, test_data$segment)
  po  <- sum(diag(tab)) / sum(tab)
  pe  <- sum(rowSums(tab) * colSums(tab)) / sum(tab)^2
  (po - pe) / (1 - pe)
}
cat("\nHeld-out assignment-rule accuracy:", round(tree_accuracy, 3),
    "| Cohen's kappa:", round(tree_kappa, 3),
    "\n(kappa > 0.6 is conventionally 'substantial' agreement -- below that,",
    "treat the rules as indicative, not authoritative)\n")

## FIGURE: held-out confusion matrix.
confmat_df <- as.data.frame(table(predicted = pred_test, actual = test_data$segment))
p_confmat <- ggplot2::ggplot(confmat_df, ggplot2::aes(x = actual, y = predicted, fill = Freq)) +
  ggplot2::geom_tile() +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = Freq)) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "seagreen4") +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Assignment-rule confusion matrix (held-out 25% sample)",
                x = "Actual segment", y = "Predicted segment", fill = "N") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()
print(p_confmat)
ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "assignment_confusion_matrix.png"), p_confmat, width = 7, height = 6)
```

TABLE: plain-English customer-to-segment assignment rules (CART; held-out
accuracy/kappa reported above).

print(assignment_rules)
cat("```\n")

```{r, results = "asis", echo = FALSE}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. RECOMMENDED SEGMENTATION MODEL -- RATIONALE & LIMITATIONS
#     (rendered as narrative text in the knitted report; the numbers below
#     are computed live from the sections above, but the bracketed
#     [ANALYST: ...] prompts require the analyst's substantive judgement --
#     segment names and commercial framing cannot be automated)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("## Recommended Segmentation Model\n\n")
cat(sprintf(
  "Across the nine 4-6 segment candidates assessed in Section 12, the recommended needs-based segmentation is the **%s** solution with **%d segments** (composite quality score = %.3f; minimum segment size = %.1f%% of respondents; stability = %.3f; %s = %.3f).\n\n",
  REC_METHOD, REC_K, best$composite_quality, best$min_segment_pct, best$stability_index,
  if (REC_METHOD == "GMM/LPA") "entropy" else "mean eta-squared distinctiveness",
  if (REC_METHOD == "GMM/LPA") best$entropy else best$distinctiveness_eta_sq
))

cat("### Segment sizes\n\n")
print(knitr::kable(rec_size, col.names = c("Segment", "N", "% of sample")))
cat("\n\n")

cat("### Rationale\n\n")
cat(sprintf(
  "This solution was selected because it had the highest composite quality score among 4-6 segment candidates with no segment below the %d%% minimum-viable-size threshold, balancing size adequacy, distinctiveness/separation, stability and interpretability (see 'Quality Assessment' table). The held-out customer-to-segment assignment rules (Section 14) achieve %.1f%% accuracy (Cohen's kappa = %.2f) on a 25%% held-out sample, indicating the segmentation can be operationalised with a simple decision tree rather than requiring every future customer to be re-clustered from scratch.\n\n",
  MIN_VIABLE_SEGMENT_PCT, tree_accuracy * 100, tree_kappa
))
cat("### Segment personas\n\n")
# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): this block previously had an
# `if (segment_labels_valid) {...}` branch containing a hard-coded
# persona_desc vector written for an OLDER GMM/LPA k=4 solution from a prior
# version of this script. segment_labels_valid is hardcoded FALSE for this
# hierarchical variant (Section 13b), so that branch could never execute --
# but it sat in the file describing a solution that does not match this
# script's actual recommendation (K-means k=4 in the current run, not
# GMM/LPA k=4), which is a latent trap for a future maintainer who flips
# segment_labels_valid without checking whether the persona text still
# applies. Removed rather than left dead: if/when WS1-needs-specific
# personas are deliberately written for a CURRENT recommended solution, add
# them behind a fresh, explicitly-named guard (not this one) rather than
# resurrecting this block.
# REPLACED (2026-08-10, critical-analysis pass): the block above only
# ever removed the OLD stale persona text (see comment history above) and
# left a manual [ANALYST: ...] prompt in its place -- meaning no persona
# text at all existed for the current recommended solution. This version
# keeps the genuinely-judgement-requiring parts authored (persona names in
# SEGMENT_THEMES above; the one interpretive sentence per segment below),
# but grounds every FACTUAL claim -- which two need themes define each
# segment, and each segment's firm-size profile -- in objects already
# computed live earlier in this script (rec_profile/FACTOR_THEMES from
# Section 13b, firmo_size_summary from Section 13c), so those numbers
# self-update on re-knit even if the authored sentences eventually need a
# fresh look. Guarded by segment_labels_valid (Section 13b) exactly like
# the rest of the persona-labelling logic -- if a future re-knit changes
# the recommended solution, this falls back to a generic prompt instead of
# silently mislabelling a different result.
if (segment_labels_valid) {
  full_item_label <- function(sc) {
    rows <- reduction_obj$score_item_map[reduction_obj$score_item_map$score_col == sc, ]
    if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(sc)
    rows$item_label[which.max(abs(rows$loading))]
  }
  # BUGFIX (2026-08-10, caught on visual QA of the first re-knit after this
  # feature was added): ranking across ALL num_cols let F3_Factor1
  # (alpha=0.263, essentially noise) and ProviderPerception_Factor1
  # (alpha=0.621, below the Nunnally floor) surface as a segment's
  # top-ranked "defining need" -- not because that segment has a genuinely
  # elevated need there, but because a near-zero value on an unreliable
  # factor can still rank highest when every reliable factor is deeply
  # negative for that segment (this happened for 3 of 4 segments on the
  # first re-knit, incl. F3_Factor1 ranking #1 for one segment). Restrict
  # the defining-need ranking to the reliable factors only
  # (reduction_obj$score_reliability), same reliability bar already used
  # everywhere else in this script (ablation check, Limitations text) --
  # falls back to the full set only if fewer than 4 factors are reliable
  # (not the case here: 6 of 8 are), so ranking never silently breaks.
  reliable_cols <- reduction_obj$score_reliability$score_col[reduction_obj$score_reliability$reliable]
  rank_cols <- if (length(reliable_cols) >= 4) reliable_cols else num_cols
  if (length(reliable_cols) < 4) {
    cat("NOTE: fewer than 4 reliable scores available (", length(reliable_cols),
        ") -- defining-need ranking below falls back to all", length(num_cols),
        "scores, including any flagged unreliable.\n")
  }
  seg_defining <- purrr::map_dfr(rec_profile$segment, function(sg) {
    zvec <- unlist(rec_profile[rec_profile$segment == sg, rank_cols])
    top2 <- names(sort(zvec, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2]
    bot2 <- names(sort(zvec, decreasing = FALSE))[1:2]
    tibble::tibble(
      segment = sg,
      top_needs = paste(sapply(top2, full_item_label), collapse = "; "),
      bottom_needs = paste(sapply(bot2, full_item_label), collapse = "; ")
    )
  })
  seg_persona_tbl <- rec_size %>%
    mutate(segment = as.character(segment)) %>%
    left_join(firmo_size_summary %>% mutate(segment = as.character(segment)),
              by = "segment") %>%
    left_join(seg_defining, by = "segment")

  # Authored 2026-08-10, grounded in the live figures joined above --
  # re-check against fresh numbers if this pipeline is re-knitted with
  # materially different segment centroids, sizes, or firm-size medians.
  persona_notes <- c(
    "1" = "The largest segment and the largest accounts by headcount, combining broad, high-intensity needs across strategic/future-readiness themes and wide service-quality expectations with a below-average need for a close, partner-style provider relationship -- consistent with a self-directed buyer that values breadth and capability over hand-holding. This segment also scores highest of the four on well-known-provider/brand-trust perception (ProviderPerception_Factor1), but that score is flagged below-reliability-floor (alpha=0.621) in Stage 1, so it is noted here as a secondary, lower-confidence observation rather than a headline defining need.",
    "2" = "Small-to-mid accounts anchored on core network reliability and value for money, with comparatively little appetite for emerging/future technology -- a pragmatic, operationally-focused segment rather than an early-adopter one.",
    "3" = "The smallest segment by both headcount and need intensity, scoring below average on every defining need dimension including relationship/partnership need (C5c-based NeedFA3 -- corrected 2026-08-22, previously reverse-coded and shown here as a standout strength; see 02c Section 3.2) -- consistent with a genuinely low-touch, low-complexity micro-business/sole-trader profile, not one seeking a close provider relationship. Workstream 3 messaging for this segment should lead with simplicity and low overhead rather than relationship depth.",
    "4" = "Large accounts by headcount but with below-average expectations on core service quality and reliability relative to their size, and this segment's firmographic mix skews most toward public-sector organisations of the four -- worth checking in Workstream 3 whether this reflects public-sector procurement dynamics rather than genuinely lower need."
  )
  for (sg in seg_persona_tbl$segment) {
    row <- seg_persona_tbl[seg_persona_tbl$segment == sg, ]
    cat(sprintf(
      "**Segment %s -- %s** (%s%% of respondents, n = %s; median %s employees, %s sites): defining needs skew highest on *%s* and lowest on *%s*. %s\n\n",
      sg, SEGMENT_THEMES[[sg]], row$pct, row$n, row$median_employees, row$median_sites,
      row$top_needs, row$bottom_needs, persona_notes[[sg]]
    ))
  }
  cat("*Persona names and the interpretive sentence per segment above are analyst-authored (2026-08-10) based on the live segment profile, defining-need ranking and firmographic summary computed in this run; the defining-needs and firm-size figures themselves are computed live and will self-update on re-knit, but re-verify the authored sentences if the pipeline produces a materially different recommended solution.*\n\n")
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "[ANALYST: name each segment and add one/two sentences of commercial framing per segment here, drawing on 'Segment Profile' (Section 13 output) and the firmographic profiling in Section 8 -- e.g. which segments skew toward larger accounts, particular sectors, or specific need factors. The existing SEGMENT_THEMES/persona notes (Section 13b/15) were written for K-means (confirmatory) k = 4 and do not match the current recommended solution (%s, k = %d) -- re-derive them before reporting.]\n\n",
    REC_METHOD, REC_K
  ))
}

cat("### Limitations\n\n")
cat("- The segmentation is derived from a single cross-sectional survey wave; needs are self-reported and may not capture actual purchasing behaviour, and cannot detect need drift since fieldwork.\n")
# ROBUSTNESS (added 2026-08-10, critical-analysis pass): the trailing
# "[ANALYST: state the actual KMO/retained-k here...]" bracket was a
# leftover template prompt -- the pipeline HAS been knitted and the real
# number is already sitting in `reduction_obj` (Section 1), it just wasn't
# plugged in. Fixed as a live sprintf() reference to
# `reduction_obj$combined_kmo`/`length(num_cols)` rather than a hard-coded
# number, so this sentence self-updates on any future re-knit instead of
# needing the same manual fill-in again.
cat(sprintf(
  "- The clustering base is the combined output of a two-stage hierarchical reduction (02d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.Rmd): 02c's 5 reliable FA factors from the 45-item WS1 pool, plus F1's and F3's own within-block factors, computed independently and combined without a further pooled EFA step. Unlike 02/02c, this pool represents information from all 80 raw items, not just 45 or 50 -- but it has NOT been tested for whether the block-level factor scores themselves combine into fewer, more parsimonious dimensions. Stage 2's own KMO on the %d combined scores is %.3f (%s the %.2f Kaiser floor), which answers whether these block-level summaries cohere, not whether the raw items cohere -- it is NOT numerically comparable, on a like-for-like basis, to either the 80-item flat pipeline's KMO=0.153 or the 45-item WS1 pool's KMO=0.973, since it is computed on a much smaller, already-reduced set of continuous factor scores rather than raw mixed-type items. Re-running the Reduction Stage with a different retained-factor count changes every downstream clustering input.\n",
  length(num_cols), reduction_obj$combined_kmo,
  if (reduction_obj$combined_kmo >= KMO_MIN) "clears" else "fails",
  KMO_MIN
))
cat("- Distinctiveness/separation is measured differently for the distance-based methods (eta-squared) than for GMM/LPA (posterior entropy). Section 12 normalises each family against its own candidates before combining into the composite score, so a candidate's separation_score reflects its rank relative to same-type candidates only -- it is still a transparent shortlisting heuristic, not a formal statistical equivalence between eta-squared and entropy.\n")
cat(sprintf("- Bootstrap stability estimates use %d (Ward's/K-means) and %d (GMM/LPA) bootstrap replicates -- adequate for shortlisting, but the analyst should re-run with higher replicate counts (e.g. 200+ for distance-based, 100+ for GMM/LPA) to confirm the final reported stability figures before submission.\n", STABILITY_B_DIST, STABILITY_B_GMM))
cat("- The customer-to-segment assignment tree is trained and tested on the same survey sample used to build the segmentation; its accuracy on genuinely new, unsurveyed client customers has not been externally validated and should be treated as an upper bound.\n")
cat("- The needs list clustered on here is inherited entirely from the Reduction Stage's item pool, correlation-matrix smoothing, and interpretability-screened factor-count search; revisiting those choices requires re-running this entire Workstream 2 pipeline, since the retained-factor scores drive every downstream input matrix.\n")
# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): previously left as a manual
# [ANALYST: ...] to-do asking the analyst to re-check cross-method ARI
# specifically at the recommended k. Section 11 already generated Ward's/
# K-means/GMM-LPA candidates at every shortlisted k (including REC_K), so
# this is computed directly here instead of left for manual re-derivation.
rec_k_cand_dist <- candidate_dist[[paste0("k", REC_K)]]
rec_k_cand_gmm  <- candidate_gmm[[paste0("k", REC_K)]]
ari_at_rec_k <- tibble::tibble(
  comparison = c("Ward's vs K-means (both at recommended k)",
                 "Ward's vs GMM/LPA (both at recommended k)",
                 "K-means vs GMM/LPA (both at recommended k)"),
  adjusted_rand_index = c(
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(rec_k_cand_dist$ward, rec_k_cand_dist$kmeans),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(rec_k_cand_dist$ward, rec_k_cand_gmm$classification),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(rec_k_cand_dist$kmeans, rec_k_cand_gmm$classification)
  )
)
cat(sprintf(
  "- Cross-method triangulation (Section 7) reported an Adjusted Rand Index of Ward's-vs-GMM/LPA = %.3f and K-means-vs-GMM/LPA = %.3f on each method's own UNCONSTRAINED solution (Sections 4-6, k = %d for Ward's/K-means). Re-checked directly at the RECOMMENDED %d-segment level (all three methods forced to k = %d): Ward's-vs-K-means ARI = %.3f, Ward's-vs-GMM/LPA ARI = %.3f, K-means-vs-GMM/LPA ARI = %.3f. %s\n",
  ari_table$adjusted_rand_index[ari_table$comparison == "Ward's vs GMM/LPA"],
  ari_table$adjusted_rand_index[ari_table$comparison == "K-means (confirmatory) vs GMM/LPA"],
  k_hier, REC_K, REC_K,
  ari_at_rec_k$adjusted_rand_index[1], ari_at_rec_k$adjusted_rand_index[2], ari_at_rec_k$adjusted_rand_index[3],
  if (min(ari_at_rec_k$adjusted_rand_index) < 0.3) {
    "The methods diverge more once forced to the same k than the unconstrained comparison alone suggests -- this divergence should be discussed as a genuine methodological finding (different assumptions surfacing different structure), not smoothed over."
  } else {
    "Agreement at the recommended k is broadly consistent with the unconstrained comparison above."
  }
))
if (length(unreliable_scores) == 0) {
  cat("- No score input was flagged unreliable in Stage 1 this run, so the ablation/sensitivity check in Section 13d found no candidate for removal.\n")
} else if (is.na(ablation_ari)) {
  cat(sprintf("- %d score(s) failed the Stage 1 reliability bar (%s), but the ablation check in Section 13d could not be run (see that section's output for why) -- treat these scores' contribution to the recommended solution as unverified.\n",
              length(unreliable_scores), paste(unreliable_scores, collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("- %s (Cronbach's alpha below the Nunnally 1978 floor in Stage 1) still contribute %d of the %d combined scores clustered on. Section 13d's ablation check re-ran the recommended %s k=%d solution without them: Adjusted Rand Index vs the main recommendation = %.3f (%s). This is the direct evidence for how much the recommended segmentation actually depends on these two flagged-unreliable scores, rather than an assumption either way.\n",
              paste(unreliable_scores, collapse = " and "), length(unreliable_scores), length(num_cols),
              REC_METHOD, REC_K, ablation_ari,
              if (ablation_ari >= 0.7) "high agreement -- not materially dependent on them"
              else if (ablation_ari >= 0.4) "moderate agreement -- a real but partial dependence"
              else "low agreement -- materially dependent on them"))
}

# ADDED (2026-08-10, critical-analysis pass): Section 6's own unconstrained
# GMM/LPA model-selection search (BIC minimised subject to entropy >=
# ENTROPY_MIN, across k = 2-15, no business constraint) is a materially
# different result from the k = 4-6 window Section 11 restricts the
# cross-method comparison to -- the pipeline's own "next steps" note (top
# of this script) explicitly warns that this kind of divergence "needs
# discussing in the methodology chapter, not silently resolved," and it
# was not previously discussed anywhere in this narrative. Fixed as a live
# reference to `k_gmm`/`gmm_fit_table` (both already computed in Section 6,
# in scope here) rather than a hard-coded "k=8", so this stays correct if
# a future re-knit's BIC search lands on a different class count.
gmm_bic_row <- gmm_fit_table[gmm_fit_table$nclass == k_gmm, ]
cat(sprintf(
  "- GMM/LPA's own unconstrained model-selection search (Section 6: BIC minimised subject to entropy >= %.2f, evaluated across k = %d-%d with no business constraint) selects **k = %d** as the statistically best-fitting model (BIC = %.0f, entropy = %.3f) -- not the k = 4-6 window used for the cross-method comparison and composite-quality shortlist in Sections 11-13 that produced the recommended %s k = %d solution. This range restriction (`SHORTLIST_K <- 4:6`) is a deliberate, documented design choice, not an oversight: the WBS Workstream 2 brief calls for a commercially actionable segment count, and unconstrained mixture-model fit statistics routinely favour more granular solutions than are practically usable for segment-based targeting (cf. Vermunt & Magidson, 2002, on the trade-off between statistical fit and interpretability/parsimony in latent-class work). The recommended solution should therefore be read as the best candidate *within* the business-relevant k = 4-6 range, not as the global statistical optimum across all class counts -- a distinction worth stating explicitly rather than leaving implicit.\n",
  ENTROPY_MIN, min(gmm_fit_table$nclass), max(gmm_fit_table$nclass), k_gmm,
  gmm_bic_row$BIC, gmm_bic_row$entropy, REC_METHOD, REC_K
))
```

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. SAVE FINAL RECOMMENDATION OUTPUTS
#     ("Needs-based customer segments that are distinct and useable" --
#     WBS Workstream 2 expected output)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
score_reliability_export <- if ("score_reliability" %in% names(reduction_obj)) {
  reduction_obj$score_reliability
} else {
  tibble::tibble(score_col = character(), source_block = character(),
                 n_items = integer(), cronbach_alpha = double(), reliable = logical())
}

ablation_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("Unreliable score(s)", "Core-only score count", "Recommended method", "Recommended k",
             "Ablation ARI (full vs core-only)", "Interpretation"),
  value  = c(
    if (length(unreliable_scores) > 0) paste(unreliable_scores, collapse = "; ") else "(none)",
    length(core_cols), REC_METHOD, as.character(REC_K),
    if (is.na(ablation_ari)) "NA (check not applicable/skipped)" else as.character(round(ablation_ari, 3)),
    if (is.na(ablation_ari)) "n/a"
    else if (ablation_ari >= 0.7) "High agreement -- not materially dependent on flagged-unreliable scores"
    else if (ablation_ari >= 0.4) "Moderate agreement -- partial dependence on flagged-unreliable scores"
    else "Low agreement -- materially dependent on flagged-unreliable scores"
  )
)

writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    "Quality Assessment (9 candidates)" = quality_table,
    "Recommended Solution"              = best,
    "Segment Sizes"                     = rec_size_named,
    "Segment Profile"                   = rec_profile_named,
    "Segment Defining Variables"        = segment_defining_vars,
    "Score Reliability Flags"           = score_reliability_export,
    "Robustness Ablation Check"         = ablation_summary,
    "Cross-Method ARI at Rec. k"        = ari_at_rec_k,
    "All 9 Candidate Profiles"          = all_candidate_profiles,
    "Customer Segment Assignments"      = rec_labels_df_named,
    "Assignment Rule Performance"       = tibble(
      metric = c("Accuracy", "Cohen's kappa"),
      value  = c(round(tree_accuracy, 3), round(tree_kappa, 3))
    )
  ),
  path = file.path(output_dir, "Workstream2d_Recommended_Segmentation_Hierarchical.xlsx")
)
capture.output(print(assignment_rules),
                file = file.path(output_dir, "segment_assignment_rules.txt"))

cat("\nFinal recommendation outputs written to:", normalizePath(output_dir), "\n")
cat("-> Workstream2d_Recommended_Segmentation_Hierarchical.xlsx (quality table, recommended ",
    "solution, NAMED segment sizes/profiles, segment-to-raw-variable mapping,",
    "score reliability flags, robustness ablation check, customer assignments, rule performance)\n")
cat("-> segment_assignment_tree.png / segment_assignment_rules.txt (assignment rules)\n")
cat("-> needs_correlation_heatmap.png / Needs_Descriptive_Statistics.csv (Section 3)\n")
